{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Correct population: all orders with status == 'completed' (i.e., not refunded)
# Conversion rate = (number of converted orders) / (total number of completed orders)

# Total completed orders by channel
total_completed = df[df['status'] == 'completed'].groupby('channel').size()

# Converted orders by channel (converted == 1)
converted = df[(df['status'] == 'completed') & (df['converted'] == 1)].groupby('channel').size()

# Conversion rate
conversion_rates = converted / total_completed

# Difference (email - paid_search)
difference = conversion_rates['email'] - conversion_rates['paid_search']

# Now, cross-tabulate channel and customer_segment to check for imbalance
# Because the channel was not randomly assigned: email was targeted at loyal customers
print("Cross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:\n", pd.crosstab(df['channel'], df['customer_segment']))

# Stratify by customer_segment to adjust for confounding
# Compute conversion rate within each segment
segmented = df[df['status'] == 'completed'].groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])

# Count total and converted
segmented_counts = segmented.size()
segmented_converted = segmented['converted'].sum()

# Conversion rate
segmented_rates = segmented_converted / segmented_counts

# Pivot to compare
pivoted = segmented_rates.unstack('channel')

# Compute difference in each segment
pivoted['diff'] = pivoted['email'] - pivoted['paid_search']

# Weighted average of differences by segment size
segment_totals = df[df['status'] == 'completed'].groupby('customer_segment').size()
segment_total = segment_totals.sum()
weights = segment_totals / segment_total

weighted_diff = (pivoted['diff'] * weights).sum()

# Print
print("Segmented conversion rates:\n", pivoted)
print("Weighted average difference (email - paid_search):", weighted_diff)

# Final answer
print("Final difference (email - paid_search):", difference)"}
